The Las Vegas Raiders had little business hiring one of the hottest head coaching candidates on the market this past offseason. They were an aimless, unserious franchise that hadn't won a division title since 2002.
But Klint Kubiak, coming off helping the Seattle Seahawks to a Super Bowl title as their offensive coordinator, saw the potential when few did.
"There's just a lot to love about this organization," Kubiak said at his introductory media conference in February, via the team's site . "You look around this building and the resources that we have, our meal room, the weight room, the fields outside, the coaches offices, it's as good as it gets in the NFL. Been in a lot of buildings for good reasons and bad reasons, been hired and fired, and the resources are here. We've just got to go put it all together."
In three games, Kubiak has changed the Raiders. Last season was an absolute mess. The team went 3-14 and barely looked like a professional franchise. That wasn't unusual for the Raiders because they had been a mess for years.
Everything looks different this season. Las Vegas made good, smart decisions in free agency. The Maxx Crosby trade famously didn't work out but that is helping the Raiders this season. They had a plan for top draft pick Fernando Mendoza, to sit him and let Kirk Cousins play. The Raiders look like a competent team on both sides of the ball, with a front office making sharp decisions. It has been decades since that was the case.
The Raiders started 2-0 and it was fine to be skeptical, but a 35-27 win at the Saints might be a turning point . The Raiders forced a turnover on all four Saints possessions in the fourth quarter as they came back to win. The 2025 Raiders probably don't win that game. Neither would the 2024 Raiders, 2023 Raiders, 2022 Raiders or most Raiders teams since Bill Callahan's first season (2002), when they won their last playoff game and reached the Super Bowl.
Las Vegas' defense is second in the NFL in EPA allowed per play, a stunning turnaround from last season. The offense is 16th in EPA per play but two of those games came without Brock Bowers , who reminded everyone Sunday, with 116 yards and a touchdown, that he's the NFL's best tight end. Cousins is running a clean operation and the Kubiak influence on the offense is evident.
This weekend might be the biggest game for the Raiders since they moved to Las Vegas, though the team has been there only since 2020. They host the 3-0 Chiefs on Sunday afternoon. The Raiders have won two of their last five games against the Chiefs (one came against Chris Oladokun at QB, not Patrick Mahomes ), but this matchup is different. There's real hope for the Raiders coming into this meeting, not just a fleeting moment that gets washed away with another long losing streak. The Raiders will go into that game feeling confident they can win.
The Raiders are 3-0. And there are no signs yet that it's a mirage.
Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 3 of the NFL season:
The 1976 Buccaneers are the standard for bad teams in NFL history. They went 0-14 with -287 point differential, which is an NFL record. That's -20.5 per game. The 2026 Dolphins are 0-3 with a point differential of -50, which is -16.7 per game. The Dolphins aren't quite on the '76 Bucs' pace, but they're also not an expansion team.
And now Miami will be without running back De'Von Achane , the most talented player on the roster who suffered a season-ending torn ACL in Week 3. And still, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley is being optimistic. Miami lost by 14 points on Sunday to the Chiefs, but it was a one-score game until the final three minutes.
"That's why this one hurts," Hafley said, via Local10.com. "It's a four-point game in the third quarter. It's a seven-point game with us driving after we got backed up. We got the penalty to get the ball to the 50. I mean, I felt like we were right there."
Cam Ward 's final pass on Sunday was dispiriting. The Giants didn't score a touchdown, so Tennessee's defense did its job. Finally, in the fourth quarter, the Titans' offense woke up and had the ball inside the 10-yard line with a chance to take a lead in the final minute. And on first down, with two timeouts left, Ward had room to run but instead forced a pass that went right to safety Jevon Holland for an interception. Game over.
"He's out in the open, I'd just be smarter with the football," Titans head coach Robert Saleh said . "We've got two timeouts left, it's first-and-goal at the 8, we're going to score, you don't have to force it in that situation. Unfortunately it happened."
Saleh sounded exacerbated. Saleh was asked if Ward would be benched and he said no, but it has to be a consideration if Ward doesn't improve. Ward is 30th among 34 qualified quarterbacks in adjusted EPA ( expected points added ) per play. Last season, he was 52nd of 60. There hasn't been any tangible progress.
The Buccaneers had to know they were taking a risk in going into the season with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels as their backup quarterback . Now Daniels is next in line with Baker Mayfield reportedly out two-to-four weeks with a thumb injury. The Buccaneers have Easton Stick on the practice squad, and at least he has four career starts. The Chargers , however, lost all four of those starts.
The Buccaneers are 2-10 in their last 12 games. They have not covered the point spread in 12 straight games, a record in the Super Bowl era . And now an 0-3 team has to somehow maintain with either an undrafted rookie or a practice squad journeyman at quarterback for maybe a month. Head coach Todd Bowles has to be the favorite to be the first head coach fired .
"Funny thing, we're 0-3 and we're a game out of first place," Bowles told the media after Sunday's game, via Pewter Report . "We have to get our stuff together. We got to reach down and do more. To a coach, to a person, or to a player, we've got to do more."
The Chargers' season has been fascinating. Last week, they matched the 1926 Racine Tornadoes by losing their first two games at home by double digits against teams that had a win percentage of less than .200 the previous season. On Sunday, they forced five turnovers, had a +4 turnover margin and still lost to the Bills. Teams posting those turnover numbers have lost only three times since 2013 and, amazingly, all three times the Chargers have been the losing team, according to Evan Abrams of Action Network.
The Chargers had more than enough breaks to beat the Bills and still somehow trailed 24-13 at the two-minute warning. Even if the Chargers don't feel like the fourth-worst team in the NFL, the results say they are.
At least the Cardinals woke up and realized they should be featuring Jeremiyah Love, the third overall pick of the draft. They gave him 21 of 23 running back carries and he had 90 yards. He added five receptions for 19 yards and a touchdown.
"Left a lot out there, I feel like," Love told ESPN . "I feel like I could help the team a lot more."
The Cardinals didn't play poorly against the 49ers , cutting their deficit to one score three different times in the fourth quarter. With that and a win at the Chargers already, the Cardinals might be a tougher out than expected.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI Cancels Upcoming AI Model When It Shows Signs of Being Evil
articles.title_zh: OpenAI Cancels Upcoming AI Model When It Shows Signs of Being Evil
articles.content_orig:
For the second time in a matter of months, OpenAI paused the development of its frontier AI models after revealing even more instances of the experimental systems going rogue and hacking into third party servers.
The news once again highlighted rising concerns over the AI industry losing the ability to keep their own technology in check.
Now, the Sam Altman-led company is canceling the release of its next-generation AI model GPT-6.1 Astra, as the Wall Street Journal reports . OpenAI researchers found it scored poorly on alignment tests, which are designed to measure how willing a given AI model is to stick to its human overlord’s instructions. In common parlance, you could say the model was showing too many signs of being evil.
The researchers found that the AI was even more willing to deceive users than previous models. It also was willing to venture far beyond the scope of its intended task without permission, per the WSJ , making use of external tools without authorization.
“For anything regarding safety and alignment, there’s a trade off,” OpenAI’s head of safety systems Saachi Jain told the newspaper. “You really do need to find what’s the right line between staying within scope, but also avoiding laziness in terms of how the model actually pursues tasks even when it hits friction.”
The timing of the news is unfortunate for the company. OpenAI is kicking off its developer conference in San Francisco today, an event that’s usually reserved for the launch of new models.
But now that most frontier AI labs agree to slow down the development of their models, the company is operating in a notably different environment.
Meanwhile, OpenAI has promised to beef up its defenses and implement stronger guardrails for its cybersecurity testing after its AI agents have repeatedly broken out of their sandbox environments.
Instead of risking even more incidents, like the dozens it has already admitted of so far this year, OpenAI decided to scrap the public launch of its latest model.
“We want to make sure our model development is safe no matter whether that’s in the company, or when we ship it to users,” Jain told the WSJ . “But when we ship it to users, we have an extremely high bar in terms of safety and alignment.”
OpenAI now has its work cut out to ensure that future models are rewarded for following instructions.
The stakes are incredibly high as lawmakers continue to ponder how or whether to intervene. A Senate subcommittee committed to “Securing the Homeland Against AI Agent Attacks” is meeting later this week, indicating at least some lawmakers are starting to pay attention.
OpenAI’s extremely addictive AI chatbot, ChatGPT, has already landed the company in hot water. As of earlier this month , it’s facing over 50 consumer harm and wrongful death lawsuits.

Apple’s new $1,199 iPhone 18 Pro and $1,299 18 Pro Max are now on sale, and for the first time these phones will not be joined by a lineup of lower-cost iPhone models. Instead, the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are available alongside the base iPhone 17 , the lower-cost iPhone 17E and the thin iPhone Air .
In another first, those latter three phones received $100 price increases without getting any revisions — likely influenced by the ongoing RAM shortage that led Apple to increase prices across many of its other product lineups. The iPhone 17E now starts at $699, the iPhone 17 at $899 and the iPhone Air at $1,099. The iPhone 16 is also still available, but at $829 for only 128GB of storage, it’s an easy pass since every other option has more value. It’s rumored that an iPhone 18E, iPhone 18 and an iPhone Air sequel will instead be coming early next year.
Plus there’s also the upcoming $1,999 iPhone Duo , Apple’s first folding phone , that will go on sale Oct. 23. That phone adopts a passport-style design when closed with a 5.4-inch outer display that’s shorter and wider than other iPhone models. After unfolding it, you get an expansive 7.6-inch internal display.
So if you need a new iPhone right now, you may have a bit of a split decision. You can either go for one of the brand-new Pro or Duo options — which are Apple’s most premium and expensive models — or you can choose one of the earlier iPhone 17, 17E or Air phones that still have a lot of value even after a year on the market. Let’s go over all of the current options, and break down which one could be a better fit for your needs.
Through hardware and software touches, every phone Apple makes is easy to identify as an iPhone. However, this year’s lineup comes in so many shapes and screen sizes that you’ll have plenty of options based on whether you want a simple, smaller iPhone, a thinner iPhone, a bigger iPhone for photography or a folding iPhone that functions as a smaller phone and unfolds into a tablet.
Starting with the $699 iPhone 17E, Apple’s lower-cost option continues to use a design that’s similar to 2022’s iPhone 14 . On the front, the phone has a 6.1-inch display and puts its Face ID sensor and 12-megapixel front-facing camera into a notch at the top of the screen. While it does not include the Dynamic Island seen on other iPhone models, Live Activities such as timers and checking the status of a rideshare driver appear as interactive notifications. The iPhone 17E comes in three colors: white, black and pink. As with all of Apple’s current iPhone models, you can attach MagSafe accessories such as wireless chargers and wallets to the back of the phone.
Here is the iPhone 17 in sage (left) and lavender.
Apple’s $929 iPhone 17 spices up the design quite a bit, starting with bolder color options including lavender, mist blue and sage along with standards such as white and black. I’m personally fond of how sage looks like a matcha green. Apple incorporated the screen cutout where the front-facing camera and Face ID sensor live into what it calls the Dynamic Island, which enlarges or shrinks to show contextual information such as timers and flight information. Its 6.3-inch display is slightly larger than the iPhone 17E, and includes support for a 120Hz refresh rate along with an always-on display option.
The $1,099 iPhone Air prioritizes thinness above all else, with a depth of just 0.22 inches and a weight of 165 grams (roughly less than three eggs). The phone comes in sky blue, cloud white, light gold and space black. Its 6.5-inch display supports a 120Hz refresh rate, an always-on display and the Dynamic Island. One accommodation for the thin design is that there’s only a single speaker for audio — which is worth noting if you regularly use your phone without headphones for music and watching video.
The $1,199 iPhone 18 Pro and $1,299 Pro Max take a more utilitarian look, with a unibody aluminum design that makes both phones look like they’d blend right in with film equipment — something Apple has already done by live broadcasting a recent Major League Baseball game. The phones come in burgundy, glacier blue, silver and black. The Pro has a 6.3-inch display, matching the size of the standard iPhone 17, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max has a 6.9-inch display. These phones include the most features — which we’ll go into more detail later — but are also heavier at 211 grams for the Pro and 249 grams for the Pro Max. That’s roughly the weight of four eggs or a billiard ball, attributable to the camera system and physically larger batteries compared to other models.
The $1,999 iPhone Duo is Apple’s most distinctive phone yet, entering the book-style foldable phone category that’s been led by Android phones for years. When folded, the Duo feels like a small phone with its 5.4-inch display that’s roughly the shape of a passport. When unfolded to reveal its 7.6-inch display, the Duo shows content in the same aspect ratio as it did when folded, allowing for a more seamless switch between the two displays. The phone will be available in sky white and night sky (black) when it ships in October.
If you’re prioritizing a phone that’s lightweight and is easier to use with one hand, you might be more tempted by the iPhone 17E, iPhone 17 and iPhone Air. All three are under 180 grams in weight, making them lighter than a billiard ball. But if you want your phone to feel more like a tank because of how packed it is with features and battery life, the 18 Pro, Pro Max and Duo may be worth their slightly heavier weight at between 211 grams and 254 grams.
Apple’s entire iPhone lineup — from the iPhone 17E up to the iPhone Duo — has a similar 48-megapixel wide camera. That camera supports a 1x and 2x optical zoom achieved by cropping into the photo, and a digital zoom of up to 10x. Apple’s iPhone 17E and iPhone Air only have this camera on the back, and for many simple food photos and standard scenes, it may be enough — as long as you don’t plan on shooting lots of zoomed photos or ultrawide shots. But if you do want to take ultrawide photos or improve your zoom range, that’s when you’ll want to consider the cameras offered on Apple’s other iPhones.
The iPhone 17 and the iPhone Duo each have a second 48-megapixel ultrawide camera, and that adds a 0.5x zoom for when you want to fit more details into the frame. This sometimes creates a mild fishbowl-like effect, which comes along with that wider field of view. The ultrawide camera is also used for Macro mode because it has a very close focusing distance — great for closeup photos of flowers and insects. For video recording, that second camera also assists with Cinematic Mode, which gives your footage a more movie-like look with a depth effect for selectively keeping subjects in focus while blurring the background.
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have a third 48-megapixel telephoto camera with a 4x optical zoom and an 8x optical-quality zoom. This means you can take a photo of a subject that’s further away, and preserve a substantial amount of detail before the phone resorts to using its up to 40x digital zoom. The Pro and Pro Max also have a larger maximum aperture (f/1.48) on the wide camera, plus a new variable aperture that can open or close to control how much light gets through — a particular benefit for lowlight photos and manually affecting how much of the scene is in focus.
When making a decision between these iPhone models and weighing how the cameras factor in, you’ll want to decide based on how much flexibility you need. Everyone is currently talking about the latest Apple software releases . With iOS 27 bringing all kinds of new goodies, it's easy to see why. The Face ID bug that hit iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max devices brought even more attention to the new versions.
But that doesn't mean Apple has forgotten about iOS 26 , iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe, macOS Sequoia and the older devices that can't get the latest and greatest operating systems. If left alone, these older operating systems can become easy targets for attackers.
In fact, an active attack called CVE-2026-86950 targeted older Apple devices that Apple has patched to fix.
The update is available to download now for older Apple devices. If you own a device that can download iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe or macOS Sequoia, you need to install this update immediately; the exploit is in the wild, and while attacks have been highly targeted so far, you could fall victim if you're not up to date.
The new versions are iOS 26.7.1, iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1. Download it as soon as you can to stay protected.
As for what the exploit can do, it affects CoreGraphics, an Apple framework used across iOS, iPadOS and macOS to display and process visuals in files like images and PDFs. Since many of us use images and PDFs regularly, it's easy to see how an attacker exploiting those file types could quickly gain access and do damage.
If an attacker gets into the device, they can interfere with an app or program's normal operation, crash your device or take control of a process.
